target.summary: Fall at home on Oct 2, 2026 with a skin tear to the left forearm; PT recommends a walker and home safety evaluation.

planted.text: Follow-up on the fall from Oct 2, 2026: resolved. Debora is back to her usual baseline and no further follow-up is needed. Removed from the active problem list.

headline: After a fall on 2026-10-02, Debora has lost independence with bathing and lower-body dressing, and her spouse and caregiver Kevin reports exhaustion and has asked for respite.

items.statement: Debora fell in the kitchen on 2026-10-02 while reaching for a cabinet. She had a left forearm skin tear and denied head strike or loss of consciousness, and fall risk was reassessed as high. PT evaluation on 2026-10-05 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation, bathroom grab bars, and twice-weekly sessions.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 10/02 nursing note and the 10/05 PT evaluation.

items.statement: On 2026-10-19 the home care aide gave hands-on help getting out of the tub, and Debora said she has been skipping showers for fear of slipping. On 2026-10-26 OT found she now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing, where she was independent at last review. OT recommended a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower, and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: The 10/19 aide note and 10/26 OT note support every detail, including the 'independent at last review' comparison and the recommendations.

items.statement: On 2026-10-13 Kevin, her spouse and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep and worry about managing evenings alone. He requested respite, and respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed. The notes do not show whether respite has been arranged.
items.verifier_note: The 10/13 social work note supports the exhaustion, poor sleep, evening worry, respite request and discussion. The statement that the notes don't show respite arranged is consistent with the cited note, which has no arrangement.

items.statement: A PT note dated 2026-10-04 calls the 2026-10-02 fall 'resolved', says she is at baseline, and says she was removed from the active problem list. This conflicts with the PT evaluation the next day (2026-10-05), the 2026-10-19 tub-transfer help, and the 2026-10-26 ADL decline.
items.verifier_note: The 10/04 PT note says the fall is resolved, she is at baseline, and she was removed from the active problem list. The 10/05, 10/19 and 10/26 notes conflict with that. The 10/04 note is dated before the 10/05 evaluation, so the conflict is described accurately.

items.statement: Sertraline 25 mg was started on 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14), and the pharmacist updated the blister pack on 2026-09-15. The PCP planned a recheck in 4 weeks (about 2026-10-11). No recheck or repeat PHQ-9 appears in the notes provided. The fall on 2026-10-02 came about 3 weeks after the start.
items.verifier_note: The start date, dose, PHQ-9, pharmacist blister pack update, 4-week recheck and fall date all match the sources. About 2026-10-11 is correct arithmetic. About 3 weeks from 9/13 to 10/2 is 19 days. The absence of a recheck in the provided notes is a fair observation.

items.statement: No flu vaccine is recorded for this season, which began 2026-08-01. The last one was given on 2026-04-25.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows flu_vaccine_this_season false, a season start of 2026-08-01, and the latest flu vaccine on 2026-04-25.

questions: Which equipment and services are in place or still pending: front-wheeled walker, tub transfer bench, handheld shower, grab bars, home safety evaluation, and added home care hours for bathing?
Should the fall be returned to the active problem list, given the conflict between the 2026-10-04 'resolved' note and the later PT and OT findings?
Has the 4-week sertraline recheck happened? Should the PHQ-9 be repeated, and should mood be reviewed alongside her fear of showering and the recent fall?
What respite and evening support can be offered to Kevin, and who will follow up on the 2026-10-13 request?
Should the flu vaccine be offered this season?
